correctness.rationale: The four binary factors are distinct; a quartic singularity would have z=0 and a repeated binary root. On each line the restriction is −z⁴, and in a chart at a contact the two relevant factors are u and u−v⁴. Completing the square turns their product into the A_7 form. The concurrence point is off the quartic and has a homogeneous ordinary fourfold germ. For f=H(H−z⁴), Euler gives xH_x+yH_y=4H; the displayed degree-three and degree-four syzygies have cross product −∇f, an exact Saito certificate. A projectivity preserves the uniquely characterized quartic and concurrence point. Its lower shear has coefficient −4c³ℓ in z³ in the transformed quartic, so it vanishes. Binary roots then classify the curves and each root permutation has four central lifts. The six cross-ratio transforms are all the reorderings modulo the Klein four kernel; harmonic and equianharmonic orbit sizes are three and two. The degree-six j-map has exactly these fibers, counting multiplicity (the exceptional fibers have squared harmonic factors or cubed equianharmonic factors). A binary change of variables identifies the harmonic form with x⁴+y⁴ up to scalar. The Fermat quartic has 96 projectivities: its Hessian forces a permutation of the three coordinate lines; the diagonal choices modulo scalars number 16. The marked union has 32. The frozen exact symbolic script was inspected but not run; its examples cannot replace the all-parameter proof.

Badr–Harui describe the plane normal form and kernel at a unique outer Galois point. This is an exact match to the mechanism of the generic marked cover, not a direct whole-curve theorem at the harmonic Fermat case. The harmonic marking requires stabilizing the chosen pencil, not assuming its deck group is normal in the full Fermat group.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither an unmarked quartic table nor the unique-point hypothesis alone determines the harmonic marked case. Using the stabilizer of the marked pencil, however, puts every parameter into the same standard cover calculation; the old freeness theorem already provides the remaining freeness assertion.

evidence: For a base map [A] taking one branch set to the other, equal Kummer weights reduce the lift condition to H_μ(Au)=αH_λ(u); choose c⁴=α. It is projective and carries the branch line fibers. Conversely every marked projectivity acts on the pencil and must map the branch set; the kernel consists of the four deck transformations. These all commute with the homogeneous lifts. The full group formula is the resulting Kummer lift written in the given plane coordinates.

The classical four-point moduli gives six cross-ratio expressions and the j-line; its stabilizers have sizes 4, 8, 12. Multiplying by the known deck order four gives 16,32,48; comparing 32 with the established Fermat 96 gives the index three without a new invariant calculation.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The extra component structure makes the identification of the relevant cover intrinsic, rather than imposing a new constraint on it. The coefficient comparison is a direct coordinate proof of this correspondence. The exact j-line, jumps, and harmonic index follow without an additional moduli or stabilizer classification.

evidence: Projecting from the common point P gives the cyclic degree-four cover. The marked lines are precisely the fibers over its four simple, equally weighted branch points, and conversely the four lines intrinsically recover P and the projection pencil.

The standard Kummer model has all four exponents one after taking infinity off the branch divisor. On P¹ any two rational Kummer functions with the same divisor modulo four differ by a scalar times a fourth power. The field is C, so the scalar is also a fourth power.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The cyclic cover with this equal monodromy profile is uniquely determined by the unordered branch configuration. Equivalences of covers of the base up to projectivity preserve the distinguished fibers; isomorphisms of smooth plane quartics are projective by the canonical embedding. Thus the two moduli problems coincide, not merely share an invariant.

originality.rationale: Not shown to be a verbatim duplicate of an all-parameter reducible-curve paper. Rather, the all-parameter marked moduli and stabilizer calculation is a mechanical instance of equal-character cyclic-cover and four-point branch-divisor classification, on top of the already proved free arrangement. The extra four lines specify exactly the cover and add no independent marking beyond the branch fibers. Existing work also treats the harmonic and equianharmonic arrangements individually.
residual_risks: The paper titled Combinatorial enumeration of cyclic covers of P¹ was not obtained in full; the publisher-mirror route for Kontogeorgis's 1999 cyclic-extension paper also failed. Neither access limitation is a basis for failure.
Exact priority for the formulation as a reducible degree-eight arrangement has not been established. The rejection is by implication, not a claim of verbatim earlier publication.

value.rationale: The natural moduli and stabilizer questions are well motivated. Here the reducible marking is exactly a distinguished cyclic projection, so the invariant and exceptional orders are routine transports of the equal-weight four-point branch data to an already known free construction. The index-three comparison is the same group count against Fermat's established order. No independently unresolved classification or new group invariant remains in the frozen claim.
